main_body: Beehive thatched hut: a large conical straw roof (rows ~2-56) over a clay wall (rows ~57-78) with an arched doorway
top_band: The thatch roof slope is the top surface. Down the centre column it runs from the roof tip at row 2 to the eave around row 56, as light/mid ochre bands (#d8bb68, #bc9a45). It ends in a dark eave row before the wall.
evidence: The big roof slope reads as a horizontal-ish top surface, like the reference house roofs. The wall below is a separate vertical face (brown clay) with a stone base. A dark eave band at rows ~56-58 separates roof from wall and shades the wall top. The door has an inset frame and dark interior. No isometric side face. Roof and wall both satisfy the 3/4 contract.

style.evidence: The thatch has about 4-5 tones, with course lines and per-straw dashes, and the outline is dark brown, tinted to match the material, so it is not a sticker look. It is still thinner than the references: 31 distinct colours against 66 and 185, and a median of 8 colours per tile against 11 and 18. The thatch coursing repeats mechanically, and the clay wall and door interior contain flat areas (12% flat-fill coverage against 0% for both references). Next to the references it looks flatter and less rich.
